text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's canary, p95 for /chat (tier:gold) jumped ~30% for long-context flows (seq_len > 4k). I ran a profiler and have a few hypotheses.

Jorge: Can you paste the numbers? is this kernel switch or batching-related? :eyes: @Maya

Maya: Short summary from the run: 
- p95 baseline (canary off): 180ms
- p95 canary build: 235ms
- KV cache miss ratio for those routes increased 12% -> 38%
- microbatch median size moved 4 -> 13 for those requests
- fallback to slow attention kernel happens for tokens > 2048 in the current selector

Maya: Profiler traces show two correlated effects: microbatch growth (batch formation greedily absorbing long requests) + KV miss churn when different conversations share microbatch windows. Both increase per-token work and latency variance.

Anya: That matches what I saw in the queue sampler traces. The batcher is extending the batching window to hit throughput targets which inadvertently lets large requests block smaller ones. We should try queue-separation or token-aware preemption.

Jorge: Agreed. Proposed quick experiment: implement a latency-governor that enforces a per-route token-budget target and splits incoming requests that would exceed the remaining budget for the current batch. Pseudoconfig: 

```yaml
route: /chat
tier: gold
token_budget_governor: latency_governor_v1
settings:
  p95_ms_target: 220
  min_token_slice: 64
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  adapt_mode: conservative
```

Maya: I like token slicing. Also want the governor to be tier-aware: gold should favor lower p95 at cost of throughput, bronze can be more aggressive.

Samir: KV cache note — when you slice, ensure KV cache affinity is preserved. If we split a request mid-stream into microbatches across different workers, we lose local KV hits and cause remote fetches/evictions. That could explain the 38% miss jump. We should prefer local continuation for split slices (same worker preference) or pre-warm KV entries for predicted continuation.

Anya: For the queue policy we can add a token-weighted priority: requests with token_count <= 256 get high priority and are batched first. Long requests get a separate 'bulk' queue that only fills slots when no short requests are pending. This keeps p95 tight for the majority.

Maya: Good. Also saw a kernel-selection regression: the selector's threshold moved from 3k to 2k tokens in the new kernelset; that changed which attention kernel we pick. Jorge — can we add an explicit override for route:tier combos to prefer the faster kernel for 2k-4k where it actually performed better in earlier profiles?

Jorge: Yes. We can add a small routing table: 

```json
{ "overrides": [ {"route": "/chat", "tier": "gold", "prefer_kernel": "fused_attn_v1", "range_tokens": [512, 4096] } ] }
```

perf-bot: CI perf check failed on canary: p95-regression: +28% on /chat-gold (long-context tests). See build 2027.

Maya: Ok, steps I propose: 
1) Roll a canary with token-budget governor enabled (latency_governor_v1) for a small subset of gold routes (5%).
2) Add queue separation config (short/high-priority vs bulk).
3) Add kernel override for /chat gold in 512..4096 token range.
4) Instrument KV affinity metric and add pre-warm experiment for sliced continuations.

Anya: I can add queue separation and metric dashboards this afternoon. Will create a quick grafana panel for token-sliced latency and per-batch KV hit ratio.

Samir: I'll prototype KV-affinity pinning — small shim so slices prefer the same worker and keep local KV. If that doesn't help, fallback to pre-warm on worker boundary.

Jorge: I'll implement the governor and kernel override. Will add a feature-flag and a canary rollout plan.

Maya: Great. Let's aim to have the canary by EOD tomorrow. Please add the experiment plan to the perf-runbook and tag the canary with `latency-governor/route-gold-5pct`. We'll track p50/p95/p99 and KV hit ratio.

Anya: noted. I'll put the dashboard links in the runbook. :thumbsup:

Samir: one last thought — consider a small adaptive hysteresis on token_budget to avoid oscillation: increase window conservatively when p95 stable, else tighten fast.

Maya: Good call. We'll add hysteresis param. Thanks all — ping me if you need infra quota for the canary.

Jorge: acked.
